title: U.S. House · California's 35th District
area: Parts of the San Bernardino/Riverside Inland Empire, including Pomona, Ontario, Chino, and Montclair.

context.text: California uses a top-two nonpartisan primary. Incumbent Norma Torres (D) and Mike Cargile (R) were the only two candidates to advance to the November general election.

summary.text: Norma Torres is the Democratic incumbent U.S. Representative for California's 35th District in the Inland Empire. Born in Guatemala, she worked as an LAPD 911 dispatcher before serving as Pomona mayor and in both houses of the California Legislature, and she has served in Congress since 2015. She sits on the Appropriations Committee and describes her focus as federal funding for the Inland Empire, public safety and Central America policy.

background.text: Immigrated to the United States from Guatemala; her official biography describes her as the only Central American-born Member of Congress and says she lives in Pomona with her husband and sons.

Worked as a 911 dispatcher with the Los Angeles Police Department for 17 years and was a member of AFSCME Local 3090; her official biography says she led efforts to improve 911 service in Los Angeles.
Earned a bachelor's degree in labor studies from the National Labor College (2012, per Ballotpedia).
Served on the Pomona, California City Council from 2000 to 2006 and as mayor of Pomona from 2006 to 2008.

Served in the California state Legislature from 2008 to 2014, first in the Assembly and then in the Senate; her official biography says that as a state senator she worked on implementation of the Affordable Care Act in California and authored legislation to modernize the 9-1-1 system.

Has served in the U.S. House since 2015 and, according to her official biography, is a senior member of the Appropriations Subcommittee on Transportation, Housing and Urban Development and chairs the Congressional Hispanic Caucus FAA Reauthorization Task Force; Ballotpedia lists her 2025-2026 assignments as Appropriations, House Administration and the Joint Committee on the Library.
Her official biography credits her with the Central American Women and Children Act and with passing the Enrique Roman-Martinez Military Cold Case Justice Act.
Volunteered with the American Youth Soccer Organization, Big Sisters Program, Boy Scouts and Suicide Prevention Center, according to Ballotpedia.

priorities.text: Says her priorities include promoting energy efficiency and renewable energy sources, increasing investments in water infrastructure, and expanding water recycling and desalination technology.

positions.summary: Says she has consistently supported funding for California's public health care system, safety-net hospitals, and health centers, and opposes efforts to repeal the Affordable Care Act.
positions.quote: While the Affordable Care Act isn't perfect, I oppose efforts to repeal it and take away health insurance for millions of Americans.

positions.summary: Wrote to ICE's acting director demanding answers about what she described as aggressive, racially discriminatory enforcement actions against Latino residents of her district and called for an end to the tactics.
positions.quote: Latino residents are being targeted based on their appearance, not their actions. That's not just immoral—it's unconstitutional.

positions.summary: Says she has demonstrated a commitment to taking on climate change and prioritizes promoting energy efficiency and renewable energy sources like solar.
positions.quote: I have demonstrated a commitment to taking on challenges like drought and climate change that are impacting California.

positions.summary: Cosponsored H.R. 4099, the Ensuring Women's Right to Reproductive Freedom Act, a bill to prohibit interference, under color of State law, with the provision of interstate abortion services (119th Congress).
Cosponsored H.R. 3115, the Assault Weapons Ban of 2025, a bill to regulate assault weapons (119th Congress).
Cosponsored H.R. 2743, the Raise the Wage Act of 2025, a bill to provide for increases in the federal minimum wage (119th Congress).

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Appropriations (National Security, Department of State and Related Programs subcommittee), the Committee on House Administration (Modernization and Innovation subcommittee), and the Joint Committee on the Library in the 119th Congress (2025–2026).

summary.text: Mike Cargile is the Republican nominee for California's 35th District and has appeared on the general-election ballot against Rep. Norma Torres in 2020, 2022 and 2024. Born in Fort Hood, Texas, he served briefly as an Army officer and later worked in the film and entertainment business in Southern California. He describes himself as a 'Reagan Republican, a Constitutional Conservative and America First.'

background.text: Born in Fort Hood, Texas; earned a bachelor's degree in business from Columbus State University in 1987.

Says he worked in Hollywood as a writer, actor, director, producer, editor, and marketing director, and previously served as a Quartermaster Army officer before going into the Individual Ready Reserve after the Gulf War. Ballotpedia lists his Army service as 1990 to 1991.

Says he moved to California in 1991, helped run a small independent music label, and handled private-label manufacturing for Power Rangers food products; Ballotpedia lists his career experience as including president of Big Event Pictures and filmmaker.
Says he has been a coach, a crossing guard, a booster club president, a Ways and Means chairman and a church deacon, and that he lives in Southern California with his wife and two children.

Ran against Torres in the 2020 general election (30.7% to her 69.3%), the 2022 general election (42.6% to 57.4%) and the 2024 general election (41.6% to 58.4%), each after advancing from the top-two primary.
Placed second in the June 2, 2026 primary with 40.4% of the vote (51,641 votes), advancing to a fourth general-election contest against Torres.
Has completed Ballotpedia's Candidate Connection survey in multiple election cycles, including 2020, 2022, and 2024, for prior runs for this seat.

priorities.text: In his 2024 survey, listed border security, opposition to transgender participation in girls' sports and to 'the sexualization of our children,' and protecting gas stoves, gas-powered cars, food prices, and family safety as key campaign messages.
priorities.quote: I stand against boys in girls' sports, men in women's bathrooms, the sexualization of our children and racism in ANY form. I promise to protect the gas in your stoves, the gas in your cars, the price of food on your table and the safety of your family.

priorities.text: Says he is passionate about international relations with the Latino community, veterans and the military, energy independence, and domestic manufacturing.
priorities.quote: International relations with the Latino community, veterans and the military, energy independence and environmentally friendly alternatives to wind and solar, domestic manufacturing.

positions.summary: Promises to 'protect the gas in your stoves, the gas in your cars,' and lists energy independence and alternatives to wind and solar as a policy focus.
positions.quote: I promise to protect the gas in your stoves, the gas in your cars, the price of food on your table and the safety of your family.

positions.summary: Says life begins at conception and that he would not support abortion except in cases of rape, incest or to save the life of the mother.
positions.quote: except in the case of rape, incest or the life of the mother, I will never support abortion.

positions.summary: Says any restriction, registration or regulation of the right to keep and bear arms is an infringement and unconstitutional.
positions.quote: Any restriction, registration or regulation of that right, is by definition, an "infringement" and is unconstitutional.

positions.summary: Says he opposes transgender girls competing in girls' sports.
positions.quote: Mike wholeheartedly stands against boys in girls’ sports

researchNotes: Torres has not completed Ballotpedia's 2026 Candidate Connection survey; positions and priorities here are drawn from her official House issues pages (health care, energy/environment) and a press release on ICE enforcement in her district. Her budget/fiscal-responsibility page discusses tax-code reform in general terms that do not map cleanly to a stance on tax_wealthy, so it was omitted. Cargile has not completed a 2026 survey either; his priorities/positions are drawn from his most recent completed survey (2024), cited as dated context. Federal key votes and FEC finance totals for the incumbent are added separately by script. Biography gaps: Cargile has not completed a 2026 survey, so his biography relies on earlier self-reported survey answers and Ballotpedia; no campaign-site bio was loaded. Torres's official bio gives no birth year or birthplace beyond Guatemala.
